messages:
alice_infra: Heads-up — I'm putting together a validation roadmap for the upcoming GPU stack upgrade (driver + firmware + kernel). Goal: measurably reduce Xid/ECC spikes we've seen in us-west and eu-central clusters. Wanted quick feedback on the rollout checks and thresholds.

ben_runtime: Thanks — can you list the exact tests you want run during canary vs full rollout?

alice_infra: Canary = 3 nodes per region, mixed A100/H100, run for 72h. Tests: 1) continuous ML inference workload (sample sequences + batching), 2) kernel/driver error tail monitoring (dmesg, Xid), 3) memory stress (memtester), 4) synthetic long-seq gen to reproduce KV-cache churn. Full = scale to 5% of fleet for 7d then gradual expand.

carol_sre: Add automated health checks and rollback triggers please. Proposed triggers: >0.5 Xid errors per GPU/hour sustained for 1h OR >3 ECC corrected events in 30m on any node OR any RAS RESET event. If trigger hits, rollback the canary group automatically and create incident. :rotating_light:

ben_runtime: Agree on triggers. For metrics we should use these PromQLs:
```
rate(redwood_gpu_xid_total[15m])
max_over_time(redwood_gpu_ecc_corrected_total[30m])
```
and alert if rate(...) > 0.00014 per second per GPU (≈0.5/hr).

dave_hw: Quick note on firmware: there are two firmware branches for H100 across vendors. We should pin exact MMC/BIOS fwrev in the matrix. Also collect GPU BIOS logs (nvme-fw style) and vendor-provided telem. I'll attach mapping separately.

alice_infra: Good call. We'll include a hardware matrix field: model, fwrev, driver version, kernel minor. Example entries: A100: fw v1.2.3, driver 535.86, kernel 6.1.x; H100: fw v2.0.1, driver 550.10, kernel 6.5.x.

carol_sre: For the smoke test, plan to run these quick checks after deploy: 1) nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used,driver_model --format=csv 2) grep -i xid /var/log/kern.log OR journalctl -k -b | grep -i Xid 3) run a 10m generation with small model container and assert no Xid. Keep logs in GCS with structured filenames.

ben_runtime: Can we automate drain->test->undrain? Example command snippets:
```
# drain
kubectl cordon NODE && kubectl drain NODE --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=15m
# run test job
kubectl apply -f gpu-upgrade-smokejob.yaml
# undrain
kubectl uncordon NODE
```
Use tolerations so test pods land only on canary nodes.

alice_infra: Also adding long-tail logging parsing job (oncall-bot will post summaries): parse dmesg for Xid strings, group by GPU serial, and surface top-5 GPUs with highest Xid/ECC activity in last 24h. If the same GPU exceeds thresholds on >2 distinct kernels/drivers, mark for hardware replace and tag node with hw:replace.

oncall-bot: autopruner report scheduled. Will post daily summary at 07:00 UTC for canary nodes.

carol_sre: One more ops detail — replacement flow: 1) cordon & drain 2) evict pods 3) mark node as maintenance in inventory 4) swap card (or RMA) 5) run full burn-in (memtester + 6h synthetic infer) 6) return to pool. We should automate steps 1-3 and surface hardware ticket for 4.

dave_hw: For validation acceptance, require: sustained reduction in Xid rate by 70% vs baseline over a 7d window in each region, zero unexplained RAS resets in canary, and no increase in serving latency P99 > 10%.

alice_infra: Perfect. I'll draft the checklist and the smokejob manifest this afternoon, include the PromQLs and thresholds. If anyone has additional failure modes to watch (thermal throttles, PCIe errors), drop them here.

ben_runtime: I'll add automated rollback playbook to the deployment pipeline and wire the alert -> runbook link.

carol_sre: I'll update runbooks and add playbook steps for quick hardware triage and log collection.

alice_infra: Thanks all — I'll kick off the canary next Tuesday and post updates in this thread. :thumbsup:
